title: Preference harness: sampling matrix & nDCG playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes a lightweight but rigorous procedure for building reranking evaluation sets using pairwise preference labels, a stratified sampling matrix, and nDCG-based regression checks. It is intended for model onboarding (first-stage compatibility checks) and iterative regression monitoring during rollouts.

Why this exists:
- Many onboarding failures trace back to skewed sampling or weak slice coverage rather than model architecture.
- Pairwise labels are robust for human preference signals but require careful tie handling, annotator pooling, and aggregation.
- nDCG provides a graded metric we can bootstrap CIs for; combined with targeted slice diagnostics it gives early warning of quality regressions.

High-level workflow:
1) Define target tasks and relevance schema (0..3 recommended).
2) Produce candidate ranking outputs from baseline and new model for a shared input set.
3) Design a sampling matrix to cover frequency, difficulty, and business-critical slices.
4) Collect pairwise labels with redundancy and qualification. Capture time, annotator id, and confidence.
5) Convert pairwise votes into graded relevance per item using preference aggregation rules.
6) Compute nDCG@k with bootstrap CI and per-slice breakdowns.
7) Run sanity/consistency audits (flip-rate, transitivity, annotator agreement).
8) Produce pass/fail signal and qualitative failure examples for triage.

Sampling matrix (recommended columns):
- bucket_id: short label (e.g., high-frequency, tail-long, query-type:faq)
- source_split: host/eng-prod/beta-corpus/internal
- workload_repr: proportion targeted (e.g., 30% head / 50% mid / 20% tail)
- difficulty_est: (easy/medium/hard) from heuristic (token length, ngram rarity)
- business_priority: critical/normal/low
- edge_flags: multi-turn, contains-entities, numeric reasoning
- target_num_inputs: absolute count per bucket
- pairwise_pairs_per_input: typical 3-5
- redundancy: annotators per pair (3 recommended)

Sampling guidance notes:
- Cap head examples so they don’t drown out tail behavior when doing aggregate metrics. Use stratified sampling with per-bucket weights derived from production invoices and feature-eng estimates.
- For long-tailed tasks, oversample the tail by 3x to ensure statistical power in slices.
- Maintain a reserved "canary" bucket with recent production queries to catch drift.

Annotation schema (pairwise):
- Prompt: full user input plus minimal context required to recreate model responses.
- Item A and Item B: model outputs (can be same model with different seeds/configs).
- Label options: A, B, Tie, CannotDecide
- Confidence: 1..3 (annotator self-reported)
- Notes: free text optional
- Qualification test: 6 gold pairs with target accuracy >= 80% before annotator allowed on task

Aggregation -> graded relevance (one practical approach):
- For each input, we have N items with pairwise comparisons. Convert pairwise matrix to a Bradley-Terry-like score (logit-scale) or simple Elo aggregation.
- Map normalized score to discrete relevance bins 0..3 using quantiles anchored on baseline model scores. Example cutpoints: bottom 50% -> 0, 50-75% -> 1, 75-90% -> 2, 90-100% -> 3.
- Alternative: use soft relevance (float) directly in nDCG calculations for sensitivity analyses.

nDCG calculation specifics:
- DCG@k = sum_{i=1..k} ((2^{rel_i} - 1) / log2(i+1))  where rel_i is graded relevance at position i.
- IDCG@k is DCG of ideal ordering for that input. nDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k. For inputs where IDCG==0, define nDCG := 0 and log for review.
- Use @k values aligned with product UX (e.g., @1, @3, @5).
- Report mean nDCG and bootstrap 95% CI across inputs. Use 10k bootstrap samples or until CI stabilizes.

Bootstrap and significance testing:
- Paired bootstrap: sample inputs with replacement, compute difference in mean nDCG between models per resample; report percentile CI.
- Pass threshold: require lower bound of CI for new_model - baseline_model >= -0.005 for gradual rollouts; stricter thresholds for ga. Thresholds should be decided by product SLOs.

Tie handling and noise mitigation:
- Treat 'Tie' votes as half a vote to both items in Bradley-Terry aggregation, or model explicitly in BT likelihood.
- If >20% pairs for an input are 'CannotDecide', mark input as ambiguous and exclude from aggregate metrics (but keep in qualitative reviews).
- Compute pairwise flip-rate: percent of pair judgments where the majority label differs between rounds or annotator pools. High flip-rate (>25%) indicates unstable prompt/labeling or edge-case input.

Slice matrix and diagnostics to compute per-slice for each model:
- metrics: mean nDCG@k, median nDCG@k, pct of inputs with nDCG < 0.5, avg relevance @position1, top-k overlap with baseline, bootstrap CI for mean nDCG
- annotator metrics: Fleiss' kappa per slice, average confidence, time per judgment
- stability metrics: inter-run disagreement (model A vs model B flip-rate), transitivity violations count (A>B, B>C, C>A cycles)
- examples: top 10 worst-regressed inputs (delta nDCG negative), top 10 improved inputs, representative ties

QC checks (pre-aggregation):
- Gold coverage: gold pairs should be randomly interleaved at 10% rate; threshold pass >= 85% accuracy for the batch.
- Redundancy agreement: require majority agreement >= 70% on at least 80% of pairs.
- Annotator churn: flag annotators with average time 2 std devs lower than median (likely low-quality).
- Metadata completeness: no blank confidence, no missing annotator id, and timestamps within expected windows.

Operational templates (manifest columns):
- input_id, input_text, bucket_id, baseline_output, candidate_output, pair_id, pair_index, annotator_id, label, confidence, timestamp, notes
- Example row: "q-000123","How do I reset my password?","faq-high","baseline:A","candidate:B","p-987","1","ann-42","B","3","2025-08-20T14:22:11Z","candidate missing step 2"

Triage playbook for regressions:
- If aggregate mean nDCG delta <= -0.01: immediate block for canary; require model owner to evaluate top 30 worst-regressed examples and provide remediation plan.
- If delta in (-0.01, -0.005): allow gradual rollout with close monitoring and daily rerun of the evaluation set.
- If per-slice regression exceeds -0.02 for a business-critical slice: block rollout for that slice and create a focused evaluation set for debugging.

Failure modes we’ve seen in practice:
- Overfitting to head queries: high global nDCG but massive tail drop. Sampling matrix must prevent this.
- Annotator bias: presentation order effects—randomize A/B order and track order influence.
- Label ambiguity: long answers where preference depends on unspoken intent; include free-text rationale capture for those.

Remediation suggestions:
- Add synthetic perturbation pairs to target known failure modes (entity swapping, numeric distortions, hallucinations).
- Introduce model-conditional prompts for fairness slices (gendered language, profanity handling).
- Use soft labels and calibration: when pairwise evidence is weak, shrink relevance towards baseline using Bayesian prior.

Deliverables for an onboarding packet (minimal):
- manifest CSV as specified above
- annotation instructions doc + qualification test results
- per-slice metric table with bootstrap CIs
- top 50 qualitative examples (with annotator notes)

Appendix: quick checks and commands (for engineers)
- run: python eval/run_ndcg.py --manifest manifests/onboard.csv --k 5 --bootstrap 10000 --out results.json
- quick sanity: grep -E 'CannotDecide|Tie' manifests/onboard.csv | wc -l  # check ambiguous rate
- sample problematic inputs: jq '.examples | sort_by(.delta) | .[:50]' results.json > bad-examples.json

Notes and open questions:
- Should we standardize on Bradley-Terry vs Elo for all workflows? BT is statistically principled but slightly more complex to implement.
- How to surface per-annotator calibration to product owners without exposing raw identifiers? Consider bucketed reliability scores.
- Explore using soft nDCG (float relevance) in addition to binned nDCG for sensitivity to small quality deltas.
